title: Rebuilding reparation: a multidimensional theory of repair in restorative justice
abstract: This article develops a theoretical and critical reconstruction of reparation within restorative justice (RJ). Prevailing accounts have narrowly restricted reparation to material and symbolic acts undertaken primarily by the person responsible for the harm. This article advances a multidimensional theory of repair encompassing material, symbolic, relational and procedural forms and theorizes reparation as a distributed practice involving persons responsible, persons harmed, communities and justice institutions. It further situates reparation in RJ within a broader ethical and political conception of justice as the repair of relational coexistence rather than merely an outcome of dispute resolution. By clarifying conceptual boundaries while retaining normative depth, the framework contributes to theoretical debates on justice.
